title: Turn text into phones and find the speech
brief: Convert ARPAbet to IPA, spell out numbers, ordinals, years, and money, look words up with a letter-to-sound fallback, and detect speech in noise with an energy VAD scored by frame F1.
hints: p.rstrip("012") strips a stress digit, and p[len(p.rstrip("012")):] is the digit itself, or an empty string for a consonant.
Write number_to_words recursively: under 20, under 100, under 1000, then peel off millions and thousands with divmod and call yourself on each part.

One regular expression can find every token: money first, then numbers with an optional (st|nd|rd|th|%) suffix, then words. Use \d+(?:,\d{3})* so that the comma after "1995," is not part of the number.
For the longest match, sort the rule keys once by (-len(grapheme), not key.endswith('$')) and take the first key that matches at the current position.
Keep the hysteresis state in two variables, speech and a count of quiet frames, and update them in one loop over the frames.
